subject: general
question: If LCM (27, n) = 54 and HCF (27, n) = 9, then the value of n is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula: Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

27 × n = 54 × 9

n = (54 ÷ 27) × 9

n = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 27

LCM(a, n) = 54

HCF(a, n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = Least Common Multiple (LCM) × Highest Common Factor (HCF)

 Number 1: 27 Number 2: n × 
• = LCM: 54 HCF: 9 × 27 × n = 54 × 9 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 27 × n = 54 × 9

⇒ 27n = 486

⇒ n = 486 ÷ 27

⇒ n = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This rule only applies to exactly two numbers.

HCF of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (e.g., 8 and 9), their HCF is 1 and their LCM is the product of the numbers.

Factor Property of HCF

The HCF of a set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM. In this case, 9 is a factor of 54 (9 × 6 = 54).
